simple_definition: A material (usually silicon) whose ability to conduct electricity can be switched or tuned, and by extension the chips and devices made from it.
technical_definition: A device whose operation depends on variations in resistivity under an applied electric field (HS Ch.85 Note 12); US regulation: an integrated electronic device or system most commonly made of silicon, SiC or III-V compounds (15 CFR 231.115).

simple_definition: A 'chip': many tiny electronic parts built together on one piece of semiconductor.
technical_definition: Monolithic, hybrid, multichip or multi-component circuit whose elements are formed in and on a semiconductor (HS 8542, Note 12(b)); WSTS subdivides ICs into analog, micro, logic and memory.

simple_definition: A single-function electronic part such as one diode or transistor, not a whole circuit.
technical_definition: WSTS category covering diodes, small-signal and power transistors, rectifiers, thyristors and other discretes.

simple_definition: Chips that make or sense light, such as LEDs, laser diodes and image sensors.
technical_definition: WSTS category: displays (character displays), lamps, couplers/isolators, image sensors, infrared, laser and light sensors; excludes liquid crystal devices and displays.

simple_definition: Chips that measure things like temperature, pressure or motion, or that make small movements.
technical_definition: WSTS category of semiconductor devices whose electrical properties correlate with temperature, pressure, acceleration/yaw rate or magnetic field, plus actuators.

simple_definition: Chips that do the 'thinking' or control work other than general-purpose processors, e.g. custom chips and graphics/AI processors in WSTS's grouping.
technical_definition: WSTS IC category including digital bipolar, MOS general-purpose logic, gate arrays, standard cells (ASICs), and display drivers; the largest WSTS category in 2025.

simple_definition: Chips that store data.
technical_definition: WSTS IC category including DRAM, SRAM, flash (NAND/NOR) and ROM/EPROM.

simple_definition: The fast working memory a computer uses while it is running; loses data when power is off.
technical_definition: Dynamic random-access memory; a WSTS memory subcategory.

simple_definition: Memory that keeps data without power, used in phones and SSDs.
technical_definition: Non-volatile flash memory in NAND architecture; layer count (e.g. <128 layers) is used by US regulation to separate legacy from advanced NAND.

simple_definition: Stacks of memory chips placed right next to an AI processor so data moves very fast.
technical_definition: HBM: stacked DRAM with very wide interface; Gartner estimated 23% of DRAM market in 2025.

simple_definition: Chips that handle real-world continuous signals such as power, sound or radio.
technical_definition: WSTS IC category with general-purpose and application-specific analog products.

simple_definition: The WSTS group for processors: microprocessors (CPUs), microcontrollers and digital signal processors.
technical_definition: WSTS 'MOS Micro' category: MPU, MCU, DSP.

simple_definition: Shorthand for the 'simpler', often older-technology chips: discretes, analog, optoelectronics and sensors.
technical_definition: Discretes, analog, and optoelectronics & sensors (SIA/BCG usage).

simple_definition: The industry body that collects chip companies' sales data and publishes the standard 'semiconductor market' figure.
technical_definition: World Semiconductor Trade Statistics, non-profit founded 1986; members that design and sell chips under their own name report revenue monthly.

simple_definition: A smoothing method: each month's figure is the average of that month and the two before it.
technical_definition: Used by SIA when publishing WSTS monthly global sales.

simple_definition: What kind of final product a chip ends up in (computer, phone, car, factory machine, etc.).
technical_definition: WSTS annual End Use Survey segmentation: PC/computer, communications, consumer, automotive, industrial, government (incl. military).

simple_definition: A chip company that designs and sells chips but pays others to manufacture them.
technical_definition: Company that outsources wafer fabrication, packaging and test while owning the product and selling under its own brand.

simple_definition: A chip company that both designs and manufactures its own chips in its own factories.
technical_definition: Integrated device manufacturer: owns design, wafer processing, packaging and test.

simple_definition: A factory company that manufactures chips designed by other companies.
technical_definition: Contract wafer manufacturer serving fabless and system companies; does not sell own-brand chips.

simple_definition: TSMC's wider definition of its market, adding packaging, testing, mask-making and non-memory chipmakers' own factories.
technical_definition: All logic wafer manufacturing (incl. non-memory IDMs) plus packaging, testing, mask-making and others; ~US$250bn in 2023 vs US$115bn old definition (TSMC).

simple_definition: A company that packages and tests chips for other companies.
technical_definition: Outsourced semiconductor assembly and test: back-end services (packaging, test) for third parties.

simple_definition: Pre-designed building blocks of a chip that designers license instead of designing themselves.
technical_definition: Licensed design blocks/cell libraries paid via licence fees or royalties; ESD Alliance 'SIP' category.

simple_definition: Software tools engineers use to design and check chips and circuit boards.
technical_definition: ESD Alliance scope: CAE, IC physical design & verification, PCB & MCM tools, semiconductor IP and services.

simple_definition: The machines used to make and package chips.
technical_definition: Front-end (wafer processing, other front-end) and back-end (test, assembly & packaging) equipment tracked by SEMI/SEAJ.

simple_definition: Consumable inputs used to make chips, like silicon wafers, chemicals, gases and package substrates.
technical_definition: SEMI: wafer fabrication materials (e.g. photomask, photoresist, wet chemicals) and packaging materials (e.g. substrates, bonding wire).

simple_definition: A generation name for a chip manufacturing technology (e.g. '3nm'); smaller usually means newer and denser, but the number is a label, not a measurement.
technical_definition: Technology generation label; no longer corresponds to any specific physical dimension.

simple_definition: Chips made with older, mature technology.
technical_definition: US CHIPS guardrails: logic at 28nm generation or older, DRAM half-pitch >18nm, NAND <128 layers; excludes post-planar (FinFET, GAA) and advanced 3D packaging.

simple_definition: One-time fees a customer pays for designing a custom chip.
technical_definition: NRE charges for custom/semi-custom devices are included in WSTS reported value.

simple_definition: Newer ways of putting chips together in one package (e.g. stacking) so they work like one bigger chip.
technical_definition: Named in 15 USC 4651 covered-facility scope; 3D integration packaging excludes a product from 'legacy' status (15 CFR 231.107).

simple_definition: A tiny electronic switch or amplifier; modern chips contain billions of them.
technical_definition: A three-terminal semiconductor device that amplifies or switches signals; first demonstrated as a germanium point-contact device at Bell Labs in December 1947.

simple_definition: A way of making chips as flat layers on a silicon slice, which made mass production of integrated circuits possible.
technical_definition: Fabrication method (Hoerni, Fairchild, 1959) using a protective silicon-dioxide layer and diffusion through oxide windows so all components are made from one side of the wafer.

simple_definition: The observation that the number of parts that fit on a chip doubles roughly every two years.
technical_definition: Gordon Moore's 1965 projection of component count doubling every 12 months, revised in 1975 to every two years; an industry roadmap target rather than a physical law.

simple_definition: The 'brain' of a computer built on a single chip.
technical_definition: An integrated circuit implementing a central processing unit; Intel's 4004 (1971) is commonly cited as the first commercial example.

simple_definition: A chip factory, where circuits are built onto silicon wafers.
technical_definition: A semiconductor wafer fabrication facility with cleanrooms and process tools (lithography, deposition, etch, etc.).

simple_definition: A thin round slice of silicon on which many chips are made at once.
technical_definition: A thin disk of single-crystal semiconductor (commonly 200mm or 300mm diameter) serving as the substrate for IC fabrication; capacity is often measured in wafers per month.

simple_definition: The newest and most advanced chip-making technology, used for the fastest chips.
technical_definition: The most advanced process generations in volume production at a given time; SIA/BCG used 'below 10nm' for 2019.

simple_definition: A machine that uses very short-wavelength light to print the tiniest chip patterns; only one company (ASML) makes it.
technical_definition: Lithography using 13.5nm wavelength light, enabling leading-edge patterning; entered commercial production around 2019.

simple_definition: An older but still vital chip-printing machine type using ultraviolet light; subject to Dutch export controls since 2023.
technical_definition: Lithography at 248nm/193nm wavelengths (including 193nm immersion) used for most layers and for older nodes.

simple_definition: A US government blacklist: selling US technology to listed companies needs a special licence.
technical_definition: List maintained by BIS under the Export Administration Regulations; exports of items subject to the EAR to listed parties require a licence, often with a presumption of denial.

simple_definition: Government rules that stop certain goods or technology being sold to certain countries or companies without permission.
technical_definition: Licensing regimes restricting exports, re-exports and transfers of controlled items and services (e.g. US BIS rules of Oct 2022 on advanced computing and chipmaking equipment).

simple_definition: A US law that lets the President retaliate against another country's unfair trade practices, e.g. with tariffs.
technical_definition: Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974; used in April 1987 to impose 100% tariffs on $300m of Japanese goods over the 1986 Semiconductor Arrangement.

simple_definition: A US law allowing import restrictions or tariffs when imports are judged to threaten national security.
technical_definition: Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962; semiconductor investigation initiated April 1, 2025.

simple_definition: Selling products abroad below their cost or home-market price.
technical_definition: Export pricing below 'fair market value'; the 1986 US-Japan Arrangement set company-specific foreign market values for DRAMs and EPROMs.

simple_definition: When governments use money, rules or tax breaks to build up specific industries in their country.
technical_definition: Targeted state support (grants, tax credits, state funds, procurement) for strategic sectors, e.g. China's 2014 Big Fund, US CHIPS Act 2022, EU Chips Act 2023.

aliases: China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund
simple_definition: China's state-backed investment fund for its chip industry.
technical_definition: China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund: phase 1 (2014, CNY 138.7bn), phase 2 (2019, CNY 204bn), phase 3 (2024, CNY 344bn registered capital).

simple_definition: A US joint research group of chipmakers, part-funded by the government, set up in 1987 to fight back against Japan.
technical_definition: Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology consortium formed August 1987 with anticipated federal support of $100m/year.

simple_definition: How much of a chip factory's capacity is actually being used.
technical_definition: Ratio of wafer starts to installed capacity; over 90% from Q2 2020 to 2021 per Commerce RFI.

simple_definition: The repeating pattern where memory chip prices soar in shortages and crash in gluts.
technical_definition: Periodic supply-demand imbalance in commodity memory (DRAM/NAND) driven by lumpy capacity additions; e.g. 1985 collapse, 2008 declines, 2023 downturn, 2024 rebound.

simple_definition: TSMC's revenue category for chips that go into powerful computers such as AI servers and PCs.
technical_definition: TSMC end-platform classification covering CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators and related data-center/PC chips; 58% of TSMC revenue in 2025.

simple_definition: A payment for the right to use a design or software.
technical_definition: Upfront or periodic fee granting rights to use IP or software; in semiconductor IP typically charged per design or per access agreement.

example: Arm charges a royalty for every chip containing its products; Qualcomm charges a percentage of a device's wholesale price.
simple_definition: A small payment made for each chip or device sold that uses someone else's technology.
technical_definition: Per-unit fee paid by a licensee on shipments of products incorporating licensed IP; may be a percentage of selling price or fixed per unit, sometimes with caps/minimums.

simple_definition: Software rented for a fixed period (often several years) rather than bought outright.
technical_definition: EDA licence granting use for a defined term, often bundled with support as a subscription; revenue recognised over time or upfront depending on the arrangement.

simple_definition: A way of counting factory output as if every wafer were the standard large 300mm size.
technical_definition: Normalisation of wafer counts of different diameters to 300mm (12-inch) area equivalents for capacity/shipment reporting.

simple_definition: The share of each sales dollar left after paying the direct cost of making the product.
technical_definition: (Revenue − cost of revenue) / revenue.

simple_definition: How much a company must spend on factories and machines compared with what it sells.
technical_definition: Capital expenditures as a share of revenue.

simple_definition: How much a company spends on research and new product development compared with what it sells.
technical_definition: Research and development expense as a share of revenue.

simple_definition: Money spent on long-lasting assets such as factories and equipment.
technical_definition: Purchases of property, plant and equipment (and sometimes intangibles); may be reported gross or net of government incentives and partner contributions.

simple_definition: A multi-year contract between a chip buyer and supplier covering volumes, capacity or prices.
technical_definition: Supply agreement (LTA/LTSA) that may include customer volume commitments, capacity reservations, prepayments and penalties; terms may be periodically renegotiated.

simple_definition: A promise by a factory to hold production space for a particular customer.
technical_definition: Commitment by a foundry to reserve wafer capacity for a customer, typically in exchange for customer volume commitments and/or prepayments.

simple_definition: Money a customer pays a chipmaker in advance to secure factory capacity, later refunded or offset.
technical_definition: TSMC's term for customer advance payments to retain specified capacity, settled by refund or offset against receivables per agreement.

simple_definition: A contract where the buyer pays for an agreed amount even if it does not take it all.
technical_definition: Commitment structure with shortfall payments if purchased volume falls below the committed level. The term was not found in the filings read; GlobalFoundries describes 'significant customer commitments' in LTAs.

simple_definition: A customer's wafer that is sent to a packaging company but still belongs to the customer.
technical_definition: Material supplied by the customer to a service provider where title and risk of loss remain with the customer.

simple_definition: Selling services, upgrades and spare parts for machines a customer already owns.
technical_definition: ASML's term for service and field-option (upgrade) sales to its installed base of systems.

simple_definition: An official agreement letting a distributor resell a chipmaker's products, usually with protection if prices fall or products become obsolete.
technical_definition: Authorised distribution contract typically providing price-erosion and obsolescence protection, cancellable on notice, with inventory return rights on termination.

simple_definition: A promise by a supplier to compensate a distributor if the supplier cuts the price of stock the distributor already holds.
technical_definition: Supplier credit to distributors for price reductions on inventory on hand (Avnet describes 'protections for ... price erosion').

simple_definition: How many days of sales worth of a chipmaker's products are sitting in its distributors' warehouses.
technical_definition: Inventory held in the distribution channel expressed in days of sell-through.

simple_definition: Orders customers have placed that have not yet been delivered or recognised as revenue.
technical_definition: Contracted but unrecognised revenue/orders; for EDA vendors akin to remaining performance obligations.

simple_definition: A 2022 US law that pays grants and offers loans and tax credits to companies building chip factories in the US.
technical_definition: CHIPS and Science Act: US$39bn manufacturing incentives (direct funding, loans) administered by Commerce/NIST, plus the 48D investment tax credit.

simple_definition: A US tax credit that returns a share of the money a company spends building a chip or chip-equipment factory.
technical_definition: 26 U.S.C. 48D credit equal to 35% (25% before 2026 placements) of qualified investment in facilities primarily for manufacturing semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment; construction must begin before 2027; can be taken as direct pay.

simple_definition: An option that lets a company receive a tax credit as a cash payment instead of only reducing tax owed.
technical_definition: Elective payment under 48D(d): credit treated as a payment against tax, refundable.

simple_definition: Deals where outside investors pay for part of a chip factory in exchange for a share of it.
technical_definition: Intel's SCIP arrangements in which partners fund part of fab capex for minority stakes; reported as partner contributions offsetting gross capex.

simple_definition: A period when customers and distributors stop buying because they already hold too much stock, so chipmakers' sales fall sharply.
technical_definition: Destocking phase of the semiconductor cycle in which channel and customer inventories are drawn down; visible e.g. in Microchip's 42% FY2025 sales decline.

simple_definition: Assembly, testing and materials: ASE's core chip packaging and testing business.
technical_definition: ASE Technology Holding's segment covering semiconductor assembly (packaging), testing and packaging materials, distinct from its EMS segment.

simple_definition: Electronics manufacturing services: building electronic modules or products for other companies.
technical_definition: Contract assembly of electronic systems/modules; a separate segment at ASE (USI).

simple_definition: The main US rulebook deciding which goods, software and technology need a government licence before they can be sent abroad.
technical_definition: US regulations (15 CFR Parts 730-774) administered by BIS that control exports, re-exports and in-country transfers of dual-use items listed on the Commerce Control List and items subject to end-use/end-user controls.

simple_definition: The US Commerce Department office that decides which technology exports need a licence.
technical_definition: Agency of the US Department of Commerce administering the EAR, the Entity List and export licensing.

simple_definition: A US rule that lets the US control some products made outside the US if they were made using US technology or US-made machines.
technical_definition: EAR provisions that subject foreign-produced items to the EAR when they are the direct product of specified US-origin technology or software, or of plants/major components that are themselves such products.

simple_definition: A US rule that would automatically apply blacklist restrictions to companies majority-owned by blacklisted companies.
technical_definition: BIS rule (Sept 2025) extending Entity List end-user controls to entities at least 50% owned, directly or indirectly, by listed entities; suspended 10 Nov 2025 to 9 Nov 2026.

simple_definition: A licensing policy where the government expects to say no to an export application unless there is a strong reason.
technical_definition: Licence review policy under which applications are presumed to be denied; contrasted with case-by-case review.

simple_definition: A code that tells an exporter which export rules apply to a specific product.
technical_definition: Five-character alphanumeric classification on the US Commerce Control List (e.g. 3A090) identifying control parameters and reasons for control.

simple_definition: A condition that makes a company give back US chip subsidies if it significantly expands chip factories in China or other countries of concern.
technical_definition: 15 CFR Part 231 restriction on CHIPS recipients' material expansion of semiconductor capacity in foreign countries of concern for 10 years after award.

simple_definition: The EU law that funds chip research and lets governments support new chip factories in Europe.
technical_definition: Regulation (EU) 2023/1781, in force 21 Sept 2023, with three pillars: Chips for Europe Initiative, security of supply (first-of-a-kind facilities) and monitoring/crisis response.

simple_definition: A chip factory that is new to Europe in its technology or type, which qualifies for special EU support.
technical_definition: Chips Act concept for integrated production facilities or open EU foundries not yet substantially present in the Union; basis for State aid approvals.

simple_definition: Products or technology that can be used for both civilian and military purposes.
technical_definition: Goods, software and technology with civil and military applications, controlled e.g. under Regulation (EU) 2021/821 and the Wassenaar list.

simple_definition: A club of 42 countries that agree on lists of sensitive technologies to control when exporting.
technical_definition: Multilateral export control regime (since 1996) maintaining the Munitions List and the List of Dual-Use Goods and Technologies, implemented nationally by consensus.

simple_definition: US rules limiting how Americans can invest in Chinese companies in sensitive technologies such as chips.
technical_definition: Treasury program (31 CFR Part 850, effective 2 Jan 2025) prohibiting or requiring notification of US persons' investments in covered foreign persons in semiconductors, quantum and AI in China, Hong Kong and Macau.

simple_definition: Tin, tantalum, tungsten and gold that may come from conflict areas in central Africa; US-listed companies must report on them.
technical_definition: Minerals covered by Dodd-Frank Section 1502 and SEC Form SD reporting for sourcing from the DRC and adjoining countries.

simple_definition: Voluntary technical rules agreed by the chip equipment and materials industry so machines, materials and factories work together.
technical_definition: Consensus standards developed under SEMI's International Standards Program across equipment automation, materials, facilities, gases, lithography, packaging and traceability.

simple_definition: An industry group that writes the technical standards for memory chips like DDR and HBM.
technical_definition: Standards organisation (founded 1958) developing open microelectronics standards, notably DRAM (DDR, LPDDR, HBM), flash, packaging and ESD.

simple_definition: Rare metals used to make some kinds of chips; China produces most of the world's supply.
technical_definition: Critical minerals used in compound semiconductors (e.g. GaN, GaAs) and optoelectronics; subject to Chinese export licensing since 1 Aug 2023.

simple_definition: The large cylinder of ultra-pure silicon crystal that wafers are sliced from.
technical_definition: Single-crystal silicon boule grown (typically by the Czochralski method) and sliced into wafers.

simple_definition: One individual chip cut out of a finished wafer.
technical_definition: A single rectangular IC cut from a processed wafer by dicing.

simple_definition: Out of all the chips made on a wafer, the share that actually work.
technical_definition: Percentage of functional die per processed wafer (die yield); also used for line yield (wafers surviving the process) and final test yield.

simple_definition: The part of manufacturing where the circuits are built into the wafer, layer by layer, inside the fab.
technical_definition: Wafer fabrication: the repeated deposition, lithography, etch, implant, CMP and metrology steps that build transistors and interconnect on the wafer.

simple_definition: The part of manufacturing that turns finished wafers into individual, tested, packaged chips that can be soldered into products.
technical_definition: Wafer probe (sometimes), dicing, die attach, interconnect, encapsulation and final test; also called ATP or ATMP.

simple_definition: Printing a circuit pattern onto a wafer with light, like projecting a stencil onto light-sensitive film.
technical_definition: Pattern transfer by projecting light through a photomask onto photoresist, followed by development; resolution set by CD = k1·λ/NA.

simple_definition: A light-sensitive coating put on the wafer so the projected pattern can be 'developed' into it.
technical_definition: Polymer (or metal-oxide) film whose solubility changes on exposure, enabling pattern transfer to underlying layers by etch or implant.

simple_definition: A glass plate carrying the exact pattern for one layer of a chip, used like a stencil in lithography.
technical_definition: High-precision quartz plate with an absorber pattern (reflective multilayer for EUV) representing one layer of an IC design; in steppers/scanners called a reticle.

simple_definition: The full collection of photomasks, one per patterned layer, needed to make a chip design.
technical_definition: Set of reticles covering all lithographically patterned layers of a design at a given process; produced after tape-out from fractured mask data.

simple_definition: A photomask factory owned by a chipmaker to make its own masks, as opposed to an independent mask supplier.
technical_definition: In-house photomask manufacturing operated by an IDM or foundry, versus merchant mask makers.

simple_definition: The next generation of EUV machines with larger optics that can print even smaller features (about 8 nm).
technical_definition: EUV scanners with 0.55 numerical aperture (ASML EXE series) using anamorphic 4x/8x demagnification, giving ~8 nm resolution and half-field exposures.

simple_definition: A measure of how much light the lens or mirror system can gather; bigger means finer detail can be printed.
technical_definition: NA = n·sin(θ) of the projection optics; appears in the Rayleigh resolution criterion CD = k1·λ/NA.

simple_definition: The rule of thumb that says how small a feature a lithography machine can print, based on the light's wavelength and the optics.
technical_definition: CD = k1·λ/NA, where CD is critical dimension, λ wavelength, NA numerical aperture and k1 a process factor with physical limit 0.25.

simple_definition: The size of the smallest feature (e.g. line width) that must be printed accurately on a layer.
technical_definition: Smallest feature width controlled on a layer; measured by CD metrology.

simple_definition: Laying down an ultra-thin layer of material on the wafer.
technical_definition: Thin-film formation by CVD, PVD, ALD, epitaxy or electroplating.

simple_definition: Removing material where the pattern says so, to carve the circuit into the layer below.
technical_definition: Selective removal of material (dry plasma or wet chemical) through a patterned resist or hard mask.

simple_definition: Shooting charged atoms into the silicon to change how well it conducts electricity in specific places.
technical_definition: Doping by accelerating dopant ions into the substrate to set electrical properties.

simple_definition: How long it takes for a wafer to go through the factory from start to finish.
technical_definition: Elapsed time for a wafer lot to complete front-end processing (roughly 12 weeks on average per BCG/SIA 2021).

simple_definition: A 3D transistor design, shaped like a fin, used in most advanced chips from about 2011 to the early 2020s.
technical_definition: Multi-gate MOSFET where the gate wraps three sides of a vertical silicon fin channel; introduced in volume by Intel in 2011.

simple_definition: The newest transistor design, where the controlling gate fully surrounds stacked thin channels, giving better control and lower power.
technical_definition: GAAFET: channels formed as stacked horizontal nanosheets/nanowires surrounded on all sides by the gate; e.g. Samsung MBCFET, TSMC N2 nanosheet, Intel RibbonFET.

simple_definition: Moving the wires that carry power to the back of the chip, leaving more room for signal wires on the front.
technical_definition: Power delivery network fabricated on the wafer backside after thinning, connected to devices by nano-TSVs or direct contacts; e.g. Intel PowerVia, TSMC Super Power Rail (A16).

simple_definition: Flash storage memory built as a tall stack of hundreds of layers of memory cells, like a skyscraper instead of a single floor.
technical_definition: NAND flash with memory cells stacked vertically in many word-line layers (300+ layers in production by 2024-25).

simple_definition: A semiconductor material, different from silicon, that makes efficient chips for power supplies and chargers.
technical_definition: Wide-bandgap III-V compound semiconductor used for power and RF devices, often grown on silicon substrates.

simple_definition: A small chip designed to be combined with other small chips in one package, instead of making one huge chip.
technical_definition: Die implementing a subset of system functions, designed for integration with other dies via advanced packaging and die-to-die interfaces (e.g. UCIe).

simple_definition: A thin 'circuit board' layer, often made of silicon, that sits under several chips and wires them together at very high density.
technical_definition: Passive (or active) substrate with fine-pitch wiring and TSVs onto which multiple dies are mounted in 2.5D integration; silicon or RDL-based.

simple_definition: Placing several chips side by side on a shared high-density base (interposer) inside one package.
technical_definition: Side-by-side die integration on an interposer or bridge providing fine-pitch lateral interconnect.

simple_definition: Stacking chips on top of each other and wiring them vertically.
technical_definition: Vertical stacking of dies/wafers interconnected by TSVs, microbumps or hybrid bonds.

simple_definition: Joining two chips (or wafers) face to face so their copper contacts fuse directly, without solder bumps, giving extremely dense connections.
technical_definition: Direct bonding of dielectric-to-dielectric and Cu-to-Cu pads at micron to sub-micron pitch (die-to-wafer or wafer-to-wafer).

simple_definition: A tiny vertical wire drilled through a chip so signals can pass straight up and down a stack of chips.
technical_definition: Vertical electrical connection passing through a silicon die or wafer.

simple_definition: TSMC's packaging technology that puts processors and HBM memory side by side on an interposer; used for most large AI accelerators.
technical_definition: Chip-on-Wafer-on-Substrate: TSMC 2.5D platform with silicon (S), RDL (R) or local-silicon-bridge (L) interposers up to ~3.5x reticle size.

simple_definition: TSMC's technology for stacking chips directly on top of each other.
technical_definition: System on Integrated Chips: TSMC wafer-level 3D stacking platform with bond pitch below 10 µm.

simple_definition: A shared technical standard for how chiplets from different makers talk to each other inside a package.
technical_definition: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express: open die-to-die interconnect specification (v3.0 current) covering physical layer, protocol and management.

simple_definition: The small multilayer board a chip (or chips) sits on inside its package, connecting it to the circuit board.
technical_definition: Organic (or emerging glass-core) laminate with fine wiring that fans out die I/O to the PCB.

simple_definition: A new kind of package base made from glass instead of plastic-like materials, flatter and able to carry denser wiring.
technical_definition: Glass-core package substrate replacing organic core, offering flatness, thermal stability and higher via/interconnect density.

simple_definition: A chip that has been fully tested before being packaged together with other chips, so one bad piece doesn't ruin an expensive package.
technical_definition: Bare die tested to a quality level comparable to packaged parts before multi-die integration.

simple_definition: Testing each chip while it is still on the wafer, using fine needles (probes) to touch its contacts.
technical_definition: Electrical wafer probe test using ATE and probe cards; results recorded as wafer/bin maps.

simple_definition: Testing each chip again after it has been packaged, before it ships.
technical_definition: Package-level test on ATE with handlers, possibly including burn-in and system-level test.

simple_definition: Testing a chip by running it as it would be used in a real device.
technical_definition: Functional ('mission mode') test of a packaged device in a system-like environment, complementing structural ATE test.

simple_definition: Running chips hot and under stress for a while so weak ones fail in the factory instead of in customers' hands.
technical_definition: Accelerated-stress screening at elevated temperature/voltage to remove early-life failures.

simple_definition: The large computer-controlled machines that electrically test chips.
technical_definition: ATE: tester systems applying test patterns and measuring responses at wafer or package level.

simple_definition: The 'rulebook and parts kit' a foundry gives designers so their designs can be manufactured on its process.
technical_definition: Process design kit: foundry-supplied design rules, device models, parameterized cells, standard-cell libraries and EDA tech files/runsets for a specific process.

simple_definition: Geometric rules (minimum widths, spacings, etc.) a chip layout must follow so the factory can build it reliably.
technical_definition: Process-specific layout constraints checked by DRC before tape-out.

simple_definition: The code-like description of what a chip's digital logic should do, written by designers.
technical_definition: Register-transfer level description of digital hardware in an HDL such as Verilog or VHDL.

simple_definition: Automatically turning the designer's RTL code into a list of actual logic gates.
technical_definition: Translation of RTL into a gate-level netlist mapped to a standard-cell library under timing/power/area constraints.

simple_definition: Automatically deciding where every gate sits on the chip and how the wires connect them.
technical_definition: Physical implementation: floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis and routing producing a layout.

simple_definition: The final set of checks confirming a chip design meets timing, power and manufacturing rules before it is sent to be made.
technical_definition: Final verification (static timing, parasitic extraction, DRC/LVS, power integrity) gating tape-out.

simple_definition: The whole chip-design pipeline from the logic description to the final layout file sent for manufacturing.
technical_definition: Digital implementation flow: synthesis, place-and-route, signoff, producing a GDSII/OASIS layout.

simple_definition: The long-standing file format that stores a chip's physical layout (the shapes on each layer).
technical_definition: GDSII Stream: hierarchical binary layout format, de facto standard for decades, limited by 16/32-bit fields.

simple_definition: A newer, much more compact file format for chip layout and mask data, standardized by SEMI.
technical_definition: Open Artwork System Interchange Standard (SEMI P39): 64-bit hierarchical mask layout format with at least order-of-magnitude size reduction versus GDSII.

simple_definition: The moment a chip design is finished and handed over for mask-making and manufacturing.
technical_definition: Release of final signed-off layout data (GDSII/OASIS) to the foundry/mask shop; term originates from magnetic tape delivery.

simple_definition: The factory software that tracks every wafer, machine and step in a fab or packaging plant.
technical_definition: Manufacturing execution system: WIP/lot tracking, dispatch, recipe management, genealogy and equipment state.

simple_definition: A batch of wafers (typically carried together in one container) that moves through the factory as a unit.
technical_definition: Group of wafers processed and tracked together through the fab (commonly up to 25 wafers in a FOUP for 300 mm).

simple_definition: The standard 'language' factory machines use to talk to the factory's control computers.
technical_definition: SEMI E5 (SECS-II messages), E37 (HSMS transport) and E30 (GEM behaviour model) for equipment-host communication.

simple_definition: Software that watches sensor readings from factory machines to spot problems early.
technical_definition: FDC: statistical monitoring of equipment sensor traces to detect and classify process excursions.

simple_definition: Precise measurement of what was built on the wafer (thickness, line width, alignment).
technical_definition: Inline measurement of film thickness, CD, overlay and 3D shape for process control.

simple_definition: Electrical tests on special test structures on the wafer that show whether the manufacturing process ran correctly; foundries share this data with customers.
technical_definition: WAT/PCM/e-test: parametric measurement of scribe-line test structures after fab completion.

simple_definition: A map showing which chips on a wafer passed or failed tests, used to track each chip through packaging.
technical_definition: Substrate map of die XY coordinates with bin/test results, standardized in SEMI E142.

simple_definition: A common file format for storing chip test results.
technical_definition: Standard Test Data Format (Teradyne-originated, V4): binary record-based format for lot, wafer, part and test results.

simple_definition: Software that pulls together manufacturing and test data to find why chips fail and improve yield.
technical_definition: YMS: analytics platform integrating fab (inline, metrology, defect, WAT) and test (sort, final) data for yield learning.

simple_definition: A chip designer, factory, or packaging or test company certified by the US Defense Department to handle sensitive defense chips securely.
technical_definition: DMEA-accredited supplier (design, aggregation, broker, mask, foundry, post-processing, packaging/assembly, test) assuring IC integrity and confidentiality.

simple_definition: A chip custom-designed for one specific customer or job, rather than a general-purpose chip.
technical_definition: Application-specific integrated circuit; often developed with design-service firms offering turnkey spec-to-production flows.

simple_definition: A company that takes a customer's chip idea and handles design, manufacturing, packaging and testing through to finished chips.
technical_definition: ASIC service model with entry points (spec-in, RTL-in, GDSII-in, KGD-in) through to delivered product, managing foundry and ATP on the customer's behalf.

simple_definition: A reseller officially appointed by a chipmaker to sell its chips.
technical_definition: Distributor franchised and qualified by an original component manufacturer (OCM); the OCM-sanctioned channel.

simple_definition: Traders who buy and resell chips outside the chipmaker's official channel; useful in shortages but a counterfeit risk.
technical_definition: Independent distributors, brokers and online component exchanges sourcing from diverse, non-OCM suppliers.

simple_definition: A step in the supply chain where one region or a few firms supply almost everything, so a disruption there hits everyone.
technical_definition: SIA/BCG definition: a value-chain step where one region accounts for more than 65% of global market share.

simple_definition: A special gas mixture (including neon) used to make the laser light in older chip-printing machines.
technical_definition: Rare-gas/halogen mixture powering excimer lasers in DUV lithography; neon is the main buffer gas.
